findings.title: Harvest count and harvest weight are multiplied by the number of journal entries
findings.where: GET /api/plants, GET /api/plants/{id}; Plants list and plant detail pages
findings.steps: Open a plant that has harvests and give it 2 journal entries (Tomato in the sample data has 3 harvests totalling 1350 g). Open /plants or /plants/1.
findings.actual: 6 harvests, 2.7 kg. The new LEFT JOIN journal_entries in PLANT_SELECT multiplies the harvest rows, and COUNT(h.id)/SUM(h.weight_grams) are not DISTINCT. The delete-plant confirmation shows the inflated count too.
findings.evidence: API: harvest_count=6, harvest_grams=2700, but the harvests array has 3 items summing to 1350. The SSR HTML of /plants/1 contains '6 harvests' and '2.7 kg'. Bed totals (separate query) show the correct 2550 g.

findings.title: Out-of-range integer ids return 500 Internal Server Error
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (SQLite integer overflow; there is no upper bound on the ids)
findings.evidence: curl returned 'Internal Server Error 500' for all three requests

findings.title: Journal load errors offer no retry
findings.where: /journal page and the Journal section of /plants/{id}
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal fail (server down or 5xx), then open /journal or a plant page
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that refetches without a page reload
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown. Neither page exposes refresh(), so the only way to recover is to reload or edit the search text.
findings.evidence: journal.vue does not destructure refresh and renders no retry button; in [id].vue the journal alert has no action

findings.title: Journal requests have no timeout, so a hung request leaves 'Saving…' disabled forever
findings.steps: Make the API stall (accept the connection but never answer) and click Add entry or Save entry
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 s with a visible error and the button is enabled again
findings.actual: $fetch.create/useFetch are used without a timeout option. The button stays at 'Saving…' (disabled) and the list stays at 'Loading entries…' indefinitely.
findings.evidence: useApi.ts: no timeout in $fetch.create; the journal code passes none

findings.title: Retrying an add after a timeout or network error creates duplicate entries
findings.where: POST /api/journal from the New entry form
findings.steps: Submit an entry. The server saves it but the response is lost or times out. Click Add entry again.
findings.actual: Two identical entries. There is no idempotency key or duplicate check, and the form keeps the text, which invites a resubmit.
findings.evidence: create_entry inserts unconditionally; the client sends no request id

findings.title: Search over 80 characters shows a raw validation message instead of being limited
findings.steps: Type or paste more than 80 characters into Search
findings.expected: The input limits the length, or a friendly message appears
findings.actual: The page shows the error 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters' in place of results. The input has no maxlength.
findings.evidence: SSR of /journal?q=<81 a's> rendered an alert with 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'

findings.title: Long unbroken plant names in the journal feed can overflow at 375 px
findings.steps: Create a plant named with 80 characters and no spaces, add a journal entry, then view /journal at 375 px wide
findings.actual: The entry body has overflow-wrap:anywhere but the plant link does not, so the page probably scrolls sideways
findings.evidence: CSS review: .journal-feed__plant has no overflow-wrap or min-width rule

findings.title: Implausible dates such as year 0001 are accepted
findings.expected: A 422 with a reason (only future dates are refused)
findings.actual: 201 Created; the entry sorts at the bottom with date '1 Jan 1'

findings.title: 500-character limit counts emoji twice in the browser but once on the server
findings.expected: 500 characters allowed, the same as the server
findings.actual: The textarea maxlength and the 'characters left' counter count UTF-16 code units, so only about 250 emoji fit, while the server accepts 500 emoji
findings.evidence: POST with 500 '🌱' returned 201; the form uses form.body.length and maxlength=500
